metadata.implementation: Two Python subprocesses simulate future Swift nodes. Model weights loaded independently in each process. Wire format per activation-streaming-protocol.md.

reference.note: Single-process baseline includes one model load.

distributed.note: Two-process split is 1.84x slower than single-process (132.1s vs 71.7s) for this 512-token sequence. Dominated by loading model weights twice, not by streaming.

comparison.note: All reported errors are exactly 0.0: the bfloat16->float16->bfloat16 round trip was lossless for every value in this run, because float16's 10-bit mantissa is wider than bfloat16's 7-bit. This is NOT unconditional -- float16's 5-bit exponent gives it a much narrower dynamic range (max finite 65504, smallest normal 6.1e-5), so activations outside that interval would saturate or flush to zero. This run did not instrument the dynamic range of the transmitted tensor, so the precondition is unverified. Instrument max/min |x| before using the protocol at a different layer or scale.
comparison.verdict: PASS: distributed final output is bit-identical to single-process baseline
